words.gloss: medical experts who wrote the treatises

literal: Even if they exceed, even if they decrease, disease will cause, (those) which the authors of treatises, wind beginning with, reckoned as three.
translation: If the three humors reckoned by medical experts, beginning with wind, either exceed or fall short of their proper measure, they will cause disease.
modern: மருத்துவ நூலோர் வளி (காற்று) முதலாக எண்ணிய மூன்று பொருள்களும் (வளி, பித்தம், ஐயம்) அளவுக்கு அதிகமானாலும் அல்லது குறைந்தாலும் உடலுக்கு நோயை உண்டாக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet introduces the fundamental principle of traditional medicine regarding the three bodily humors: wind (vatha), bile (pitha), and phlegm (kapha). The poet refers to them as the 'three things reckoned by experts, beginning with wind'. Health is maintained when these three elements exist in perfect balance. If any of these three humors either exceeds its natural proportion or falls below it, the imbalance disrupts the body's harmony and causes disease.
